#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --time=01:00:00
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=18
#   --mem=8G
#   --job-name="glap_bol_lin"
#   --output="laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out"

# Map to Flux: 1 node, 18 tasks.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 18
#flux: --time-limit=1h
#flux: --job-name="glap_bol_lin"
#flux: --output=laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=8G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --ntasks-per-node=18 (explicit per-node placement)
# Flux does not have a universally portable batch directive for tasks-per-node.
# Performance implication: if the job were to span multiple nodes, rank placement might differ; here we force -N 1 to preserve intent.

module load matlab/R2022a
module load intel

export omp_num_threads=8

cd /home/lynch/boltzmann_solvers/mtmhbe_solver/performance/laporta/grid_study/nvib_sweep_data/

# Slurm did not explicitly use srun. If you intend to use all 18 tasks, launch under Flux.
# Otherwise, requesting 18 tasks may waste resources.
flux run -n 18 matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "laporta_bolsig_linear;exit;"

reasons: The original Slurm job requested 8G of memory (`--mem=8G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
issues: The resource section allocates 18 tasks and the script launches 18 MATLAB instances (`flux run -n 18 matlab ...`). If the intent was one MATLAB process using threads (as suggested by `omp_num_threads=8`), the resource request and launch strategy may be incorrect and could oversubscribe the node.

#!/bin/bash

# Copy/paste this job script into a text file and submit with the command:
#    sbatch thefilename
# job standard output will go to the file slurm-%j.out (where %j is the job ID)

#SBATCH --time=01:00:00   # walltime limit (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --nodes=1   # number of nodes
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=18   # 36 processor core(s) per node 
#SBATCH --mem=8G   # maximum memory per node
#SBATCH --job-name="glap_bol_lin"
#SBATCH --output="laporta_grid_study_nvib_bolsig_linear.out"

module load matlab/R2022a
module load intel
export omp_num_threads=8
cd /home/lynch/boltzmann_solvers/mtmhbe_solver/performance/laporta/grid_study/nvib_sweep_data/
matlab -nodisplay -nosplash -nodesktop -r "laporta_bolsig_linear;exit;"
